articles.title: Coaching hires, stars in different places and rule changes: Here's what's new for the 2026 NFL season
articles.summary: There are some notable differences around the NFL for the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Free agency and big trades assure that players are changing places. Impatient team owners are a cause of heavy coaching turnover. The NFL's desire to expand its reach leads to regular-season games on days of the week we aren't used to and action in new international cities.

Here are the biggest changes to note as the NFL season gets set to kick off:

If you've never heard the term "Thanksgiving Eve," you will this year thanks to the NFL. The league made up a holiday to stuff another game on the schedule. The Wednesday before Thanksgiving, the Packers will play at the Rams in a game that will stream on Netflix. Hope you don't have travel plans.

That's the biggest addition to the NFL schedule, though there are other tweaks. The opening night game to start the regular season, between the Patriots and Seahawks, will be on a Wednesday. The 2012 season opener was played on a Wednesday to avoid the Democratic National Convention. This year, the schedule was shifted to squeeze in the Rams and 49ers starting the season in Australia, which will take place Thursday night in U.S. time zones.

International games are a big part of the schedule. There will be a record nine international games this season, spanning seven countries. The NFL will play regular-season games in France and Australia for the first time.

If it seems like there was a lot of turnover this offseason, there was. The 10 coaching changes tied an NFL record for one offseason. Six of the new hires are getting their shot at being an NFL head coach for the first time. There's also two former NFL Coach of the Year winners (John Harbaugh, Kevin Stefanski) and a Super Bowl winning coach (Mike McCarthy) among the hires.

One change that is mostly impractical is a tweak to the onside kick rules. Last season, the rule that teams could onside kick only in the fourth quarter was removed. In another change for this season, teams don't need to be trailing to onside kick. However, onside kicks aren't exactly a surprise to the opponent when they need to be declared beforehand.

The other change to kickoffs is that teams kicking off from the 50-yard line due to a personal foul won't have an incentive to kick out of bounds. Before, kicking out of bounds placed the ball at the 25-yard line, whereas a touchback would put the ball at the 30. Under the new rule, a touchback will go to the 20-yard line. Also on kickoffs, the receiving team is required to have only five players line up on the restraining line instead of six, allowing up to four players to be off the line.

The other notable change is that NFL personnel can consult with on-field officials "when considering disqualifications for both flagrant football acts and non-football acts" even if a penalty wasn't called on the field.

One new stadium, one under construction, one bidding farewell

There's one new stadium in the NFL this season: Buffalo's Highmark Stadium.

Yes, it's the same name of the old building that stood roughly 500 feet away, so fans who attended a Bills game from 1973 to 2025 won't have trouble with directions. Many other elements of this $2.2 billion project, however, are much different .

First of all, new Highmark's name fits well because it stands roughly 120 feet tall, which is nearly double the old stadium height. A 360-degree steel canopy above the stadium serves two purposes:

1. It supposedly blocks 60-65% of the seats from snow and rain 2. It's meant to funnel fan noise back toward the field

That's probably a good thing because there's a reduction in seating capacity — from 71,608 at the old place to now 60,108 fixed seats, the fewest in the NFL. Full capacity can reach a few thousand more with standing-room fans added, but it will be a more intimate feel, especially with the upper sections pulled closer to the field to create a Roman Colosseum-style seating bowl .

Early fan reports have been mixed, with complaints of poor sight lines, steep climbs to the upper sections and a scoreboard that some find underwhelming by modern standards. But many have praised the beauty of the new building (with several Buffalo-specific touches), the open concourses with continuous field views and the major improvements to food, amenities and comfort. Expect it to get loud in the new jewel box.

Another franchise is downsizing its capacity — temporarily. Jacksonville's EverBank Stadium will drop to a capacity of roughly 42,500 (down from roughly 70,000) this season as the Jaguars continue working on their $1.4 billion "Stadium of the Future" renovations.

That means most of the upper deck and the Sky Patio will be offline for the Jaguars' six games at EverBank, with two "home" games in London. The team will temporarily move to Orlando in 2027 and then move back into the fully renovated stadium (to be renamed later) in 2028.

The Titans are also saying goodbye to Nissan Stadium, their home since their Super Bowl season in 1999. They'll play the 2026 season there before moving to — ready for this? — New Nissan Stadium, which is under construction close by on Nashville's East Bank.

Like with Buffalo, New Nissan is going for a more intimate feel and smaller capacity. It has already been selected to host Super Bowl LXIV in 2030.

More grass coming to the NFL this season

The 2026 World Cup saw grass installed in many stadiums used by NFL teams this summer. Then that grass was torn out.

Players tweeted support during the Cup for more grass surfaces to be used in the NFL, and the good news for them is that it's at least trending in their desired direction — minimally, anyway.

With the Bills switching from artificial turf at the old Highmark Stadium to natural Kentucky bluegrass at the new Highmark Stadium, the league is now split evenly, with 16 teams having grass on its home fields and 16 using turf. (The stadium split is 16-14 in favor of grass, but two turf-field stadiums — SoFi in L.A. and MetLife in New York — each house two teams.

One other team changing playing surfaces, the Pittsburgh Steelers, are sticking with grass but are switching the type they're using. They're going from Kentucky bluegrass to Tahoma 31 Bermuda, a more cold-tolerant variety of natural grass.

Several players complained about the old surface at Acrisure Stadium, earning an F-minus grade in an internal NFLPA study last year . Aaron Rodgers even called it "borderline unplayable" after a win over the Browns last season.

Biggest faces to change teams, with trades dominating the offseason headlines

This offseason had a specific flavor, heavier on trades and more specific to wide receivers and both lines of scrimmage.

Trades have been on the influx over the past decade, and we had one of the biggest ones in years with the Browns sending Myles Garrett to the Rams for Jared Verse and multiple draft picks. The Rams already were viewed as one of the clear Super Bowl favorites before the deal, and this only hardened that idea.

WR A.J. Brown (from Philly to New England)

DT Dexter Lawrence II (N.Y. Giants to Cincinnati)

CB Trent McDuffie (from Kansas City to the Rams)

Not coincidentally, all the teams acquiring these star players enter this season believing they're contenders.

Free agency might not have had many fireworks, but it wasn't exactly quiet either.

Center Tyler Linderbaum left the Ravens to sign a record deal with the Raiders. Edge Trey Hendrickson went to the Ravens from the Bengals, who tried to offset it with the signings of edge Boye Mafe and defensive tackle Jonathan Allen, along with the Lawrence trade.

The Panthers made two big defensive splashes, signing edge Jaelan Phillips and linebacker Devin Lloyd. Perhaps the most shocking move was wide receiver Mike Evans leaving the Buccaneers, the only NFL team he'd known, for the 49ers. And before they landed Brown, the Patriots also handed out big money to fellow wide receiver Romeo Doubs.

Notice a trend? In a quieter year for movement at certain positions, there was a heavy emphasis on beefing up on defensive fronts (and offensive linemen to block them) and with wide receivers (along with corners to defend them).

It was still a fairly busy stretch for QB movement, with four potential starters swapping unis — Kyler Murray (from Cardinals to Vikings), Malik Willis (Packers to Dolphins), Kirk Cousins (Falcons to Raiders) and Geno Smith (Raiders to Jets). But none of those players, save for perhaps Willis, are considered more likely than not to be their respective teams' starters beyond 2026.

articles.title: Browns place Dillon Gabriel on IR, with long-term outlook on all 4 of their QBs remaining unclear
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns will keep four quarterbacks on their initial 53-man roster, and it's hard to tell how strongly they feel about any of them.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns will hang onto all four of their quarterbacks for now, with a caveat. However you look at the situation, it's hard to tell how strongly they feel about any of them.

Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders and rookie Taylen Green all will be on the initial 53-man roster, with Dillon Gabriel reportedly headed to injured reserve for a minimum of four games with a back injury. Gabriel will carry a designation to return this season, allowing Cleveland to keep him without using an initial roster spot on him and potentially adding him later in the season.

Watson beat out Sanders for Week 1 starting duties after new head coach Todd Monken pared down the starting battle early. That's about the only clarity we have right now, short or long term.

Gabriel, the Browns' third-round draft pick in 2025, was largely a forgotten man until he had a strong outing in the final preseason game against New England. But Green also showed enough in that game to where the Browns might have feared what would happen if they tried to sneak him through waivers to the practice squad.

Even with all four remaining in the picture, it's hard to view the situation as a clear vote of confidence for any of them right now.

Is it possible we see four different quarterbacks play for the Browns this season? Or is this just a temporary insurance policy while the Browns bide time prior to what could be a bonanza of a QB class in the 2027 NFL Draft?

Here's where all four appear to stand right now in Cleveland:

Watson being booed by the Cleveland fans was an ugly affair for all parties. He didn't like it and spoke out, which appeared to make matters worse. His subsequent walk-back likely didn't do much to quell Browns fans' anger at being coupled with one of the worst returns on investment in modern NFL history.

Yet the Browns are steaming ahead with Watson set to start the opener in two weeks.

The Browns open on the road the first two games, at the Jaguars Week 1 and at the Buccaneers in Week 2. If Watson doesn't play pretty darned well, it will be fascinating to see how Monken handles the home opener in Week 3 against the Panthers. Would they endure more possible booing every time the offense takes the field?

We knew Watson wouldn't be cut this offseason because of the punitive contract he's signed to, which mercifully runs out after this season. But the fact that he's starting initially is also an indictment of the rest of the QB depth chart. The chances of Watson somehow returning to the team next season seem impossibly low, almost nil, but it also begs the question of what the future holds in Cleveland for the other three.

Sanders started and outplayed Watson in the second preseason game, which led to some false hope among Browns fans that he'd pick up again as the team's starter. His seven starts last season probably delivered more bad than good, but the Browns appeared to play better last season with Sanders than with the other quarterbacks.

It's fair to wonder whether this is Sanders' final season in Cleveland. The Browns gave him a chance to win the starting job, and he couldn't do it. Sanders presumably would be the first option to replace Watson midseason, although that's less clear after Gabriel performed better in the third preseason game than either Watson or Sanders did in the first two.

Sanders has a very affordable contract, with salary-cap hits between $1.1 million and $1.3 million the next three seasons. He's 24 years old and has some moldable talent — but how much?

The Browns must ask whether the potential upside outweighs the negatives, as he continues to try to master the finer points of quarterbacking. To date, he hasn't.

The Browns likely won't make any long-term decisions on Sanders' future until after the season, of course, and it would stand to reason he could receive multiple starts. That would allow him to rewrite his script and give himself a chance to stick in Cleveland. Browns fans appear ready and willing to embrace any quarterback not named Watson to take the job and run with it, even if the possibility the team drafts a quarterback in Round 1 next spring feels fairly high.

Gabriel appeared to lock up a spot on the roster with his 12-of-15, 186-yard, 3-TD half in the preseason finale, although the Browns found a way to circumvent committing a roster spot by stashing him on IR for now.

General manager Andrew Berry invested a third-round selection on Gabriel just over a year ago, so cutting him never felt like a realistic option. It's also hard to imagine there was much trade chatter involving Gabriel, even with the final outing Thursday, considering how little he played this summer.

Perhaps that final preseason performance allowed Gabriel a chance to impact the Browns in the longer term. Some might view him as possessing a career-backup ceiling, but the Browns are looking for any type of stability at the position.

If Watson struggles early, Sanders theoretically would be next in line. But if Gabriel is added to the roster later in the season, he could be in line for playing time if both Watson and Sanders fail to keep the starting job.

It's also fair to question why Monken appeared to initially pare down the starting options to Watson and Sanders. Some have speculated that Monken always seemed to want Watson and never viewed Gabriel as starting-caliber. Has anything changed now? That's unclear.

If the Browns at the very least believe that Gabriel has a high enough floor, and he performs well enough if and/or when that chance comes, he might end up having higher odds of being the backup or bridge starter to begin the 2027 season, depending on who the Browns draft.

Green was a sixth-rounder for a reason: He was a gifted but flawed project. At nearly 6-foot-6 and 225 pounds, with outstanding athleticism and arm talent, Green has all the tools you could want at the position. But his inconsistent college tape dropped him in the draft for a reason.

The Browns selected him this spring amid their cloudy QB situation, and it was fair then to think "why not?" The problem in a situation like this, of course, is time and opportunity. The Browns were running a deficit on both.

"There's just not enough reps," Monken lamented recently, and he's right.

Now Green stands as the third QB for at least the first four games.

To the Browns' credit, they gave Green some chances against the Bills in joint practices, followed by clean-up duty in the preseason game at New England. Green reportedly comported himself well in both settings, which was a pleasant development. It also might have been encouraging enough to where the Browns felt uneasy about trying to sneak him through waivers.

Prior to that, Green almost never received team-period snaps while Watson and Sanders battled. Hence the problem with the crowded QB room.

Monken has given Green some praise after his limited chances.

"That dude is smart as heck," Monken said. "… I love that dude. All he does is work, [with a] smile on his face."

The path to 2026 playing time appeared to be muddled prior to Gabriel landing on IR. Is there a chance Green's running ability could give him a path to playing time at some point? You can't rule it out, especially in any worst-case scenario that might unfold.

If the Browns stick with the plan and determine they can afford to roster him all season, it's possible that Green could stick as the second or third QB next season.

articles.title: How Aaron Donald's NFL Return Impacts Rams' Super Bowl Odds, Comeback Player of the Year Race
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams are now the prohibitive betting favorites to win the Super Bowl after Aaron Donald came out of retirement and rejoined the team on Sunday, pairing with Myles Garrett to give them a frightening defensive line.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are now the prohibitive betting favorites to win the Super Bowl after Aaron Donald came out of retirement and rejoined the team on Sunday, pairing with Myles Garrett to give them a frightening defensive line.

Following the Rams in the Super Bowl odds are the Buffalo Bills (+1000), the defending-champion Seattle Seahawks (+1100), the Baltimore Ravens (+1300) and four teams at +1700 (Detroit Lions, Los Angeles Chargers, Kansas City Chiefs, Houston Texans), per FanDuel .

The Rams have had quite the offseason, adding Garrett, Donald, Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. Not bad for a team that reached the NFC Championship Game last season, losing a thriller to the Seahawks. The betting public clearly is very high on L.A. heading into the 2026 season.

And Donald will be a popular pick to Comeback Player of the Year, though questions remain how he will hold up after two seasons away from the sport.

articles.title: Aaron Donald makes major decision on an NFL return
articles.summary: After an offseason filled with multiple signs indicating an NFL return, Aaron Donald has made his choice on the matter.
articles.body:
After an offseason filled with intrigue regarding whether or not an NFL return was in the works for legendary defensive tackle Aaron Donald, he has finally made his decision – and it's good news for fans of the Los Angeles Rams .

Rejoin the Rams for one more season, coming out of retirement to sign a one-year, $20 million deal. Donald has decided to re-join the Rams for one more season, coming out of retirement to sign a one-year, $20 million deal, with playoff incentives that could eventually boost the contract to $30 million. He will now play in the league for the first time since the 2023 season.

Donald returns to join defensive end Myles Garrett on the team's defensive line after the Rams acquired him via a trade with the Cleveland Browns this offseason. Garrett is the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year and set a new league record for sacks in a single season last year, recording 23 sacks in 2025.

After the Rams acquired Garrett this offseason, Donald reportedly began a "very strict, regimented process that was similar to what he did when he played" as he explored a potential return. Donald is a three-time Defensive Player of the Year and an eight-time first-team All-Pro selection. Both men are viewed among the top defensive linemen in NFL history and will now have the opportunity to play together for the first time.

Vegas oddsmakers already had the Rams as favorites to capture Super Bowl LXI before Donald's return was announced. Now, the Rams will be the only team to begin the season with multiple players who have won multiple Defensive Player of the Year awards.

articles.title: 2 Jaguars' 2025 draft picks left off 2026 53-man roster
articles.summary: Two 2025 NFL draft picks made by the Jaguars are not on the initial 2026 53-man roster.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars released their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season, and not included were two 2025 draft picks.

Linebackers Jack Kiser and Jalen McLeod have been waived and are subject to waivers.

Kiser, a fourth-round pick in 2025, filled a special-teams-heavy role as a rookie. A knee injury, however, sidelined him for nearly all of training camp.

McLeod, a sixth-round selection in 2025, missed his rookie season due to injury. His play throughout the summer was up and down, although he did seem to come on strong at the end.

Making up the Jaguars linebacker room are Foye Oluokun, Ventrell Miller, Branson Combs, Dennis Gardeck, and Jahlani Tavai.

articles.title: Updated 2027 NFL mock draft as 2026 preseason concludes
articles.summary: Football season is officially here! So here is our latest 2027 NFL mock draft, covering the entire first round.
articles.body:
The NFL preseason is now in the books, so the next time you see your favorite team play, it will count as real, authentic, genuine football. It will not be a football like substance. Yesterday was week zero of college football, and kudos to the NCAA on that, as no other sport has a "week zero."

So wear your Billy Corgan/Smashing Pumpkins shirts in celebration of that. Football season is officially here! So here is our latest 2027 NFL mock draft, covering the entire first round.

Click the player's name, where highlighted, for a link to a feature on that specific prospect.

1. Miami Dolphins , Arch Manning , QB, Texas

If you thought the hype for him last football season was massive, well, get ready, because even more hoopla is coming up this term.

2. Arizona Cardinals, Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State

Best overall prospect, regardless of position, in this class. The OSU = Wide Receiver U tradition continues.

This is a classic case of someone who benefited greatly from getting to play in the NIL era . He still gets paid handsomely while staying in school, and at the same time, keeps grow and developing. In addition to his elite level on-the-field traits, Moore seems to also have great character off of it.

His work in raising awareness for mental health issues, and his remarks about what he learned during his trip to Japan convey the high level of leadership skills that he possesses.

4. Cleveland Browns Colin Simmons, EDGE, Texas

Brownies could clearly use a new edge, to replace the departed Myles Garrett

5. Tennessee Titans, Dylan Stewart, EDGE, South Carolina

Another key piece added to the major rebuilding project in Nashville.

6. Las Vegas Raiders, Omarion Miller, WR, Arizona State

Vegas will grab a top flight receiver, to pair with QB Fernando Mendoza, somewhere in the early portion of this draft.

7. Atlanta Falcons, Trevor Goosby, OT, Texas

Given how we have three Longhorns going in the top seven, is Texas back? Finally? And do we actually mean it this time?

8. New Orleans Saints , Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame

Our first off-script pick, Saints' primary need is edge rusher, but there is no one rated high enough on the big board to go here. So we see them going best player available.

9 Carolina Panthers , Jordan Seaton, OT, LSU

They have selected offense in the first round, five straight years. Why not make it six?

10 Pittsburgh, David Stone, DT, Oklahoma

Steelers are looking to rebuild are on the D-line, and if Stone falls to then here, they should nab him.

11 NY Giants, Ellis Robinson IV, CB, Georgia

Big blue definitely needs some help in pass defense.

12. Washington Commanders , Cam Coleman, WR, Texas

Giving Jayden Daniels another major weapon to work with would help him reach his full potential. And if/when that happens, we'll truly see how far he could carry the Commanders.

13. Minnesota Vikings , Julian Sayin , QB, Ohio State

The Vikings are ready to move on from JJ McCarthy, as Kyler Murray was named the starter for this season. He might just be a stop gap solution though. #JustSayin

14. NY Jets via the Indianapolis Colts, Tae Johnson, S, Notre Dame

Gang green didn't record an interception last season, so they need to focus on finding a playmaker in the secondary.

15. Jacksonville Jaguars, KJ Bolden, S, Georgia

This seems like a perfect fit all around- fills team need and gets picked within the range that he's slotted.

16. NY Jets via Dallas Cowboys, Justin Scott, DL, Miami

Jets have so many needs...good thing they have three first rounders in 2027.

17. Cincinnati Bengals, Zabien Brown, CB, Alabama

With pending free agents at the corner position, Cincy needs to plan ahead.

18. Chicago Bears, Kewan Lacy, RB, Ole Miss

No matter where they'll be running the football- Hammond, IN or Arlington Heights, IL or still on the shores of Lake Michigan, the Monsters of the Midway could use an upgrade at tailback position.

19. Tampa Bay Buccaneers , CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame

It's a contract year for Baker Mayfield, and if he does indeed walk, then the Buccos need a new franchise QB.

20. Houston Texans , Sammy Brown, LB, Clemson

Brown looks poised to have a big season and boost his stock.

21. Dallas Cowboys via Green Bay, Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana

Maybe the next blue chip prospect that the great Curt Cignetti will coach into a high first round talent?

22. Denver Broncos, A'Mauri Washington, DT, Oregon

This is a name to keep an extra eye on- he should, at least in theory, shoot up the board during the season.

23. Detroit Lions , Drew Mestemaker , QB, Oklahoma State

Yes, we're thinking the Lions might soon max out on the Jared Goff era. And once that window closes, they'll need to move on.

24. New England Patriots, Kenyatta Jackson, EDGE, Ohio State

A major disruptive force, who announces his presence, with authority, in opposing backfields.

25. Philadelphia Eagles, K.J. Duff , WR, Rutgers

Philly needs to find an A.J. Brown replacement. Huff had a big 2025, which included a viral one-handed grab against PSU and a 240+ yard performance against Purdue. In an exclusive with The Sports Bank , Duff discussed the NFL stars he models his game after:

"If I turn on the NFL film, I like to watch Mike Evans. One of the most consistent receivers ever, and Drake London as well. I think the body frame, body type. I enjoy watching him."

26. L.A. Chargers, Will Echoles, DT, Ole Miss

He may not fall this far down the board, but if he does, you can't pass him up.

27. San Francisco 49ers, Ryan Coleman-Williams , WR, Alabama

This is our first real wild card, high risk/reward pick.

28. Kansas City Chiefs, Jeremiah Johnson , TE, Oregon

Could Oregon produce the first tight end off the board in back to back seasons? Kenyon Sadiq was the first TE selected this past April and Johnson discussed what he learned from his predecessor.

"Just his drive for the game," Johnson said exclusively to The Sports Bank . "He just wants to get better at in every aspect of the game.

"That's from on the field to knowing the playbook to off the field to getting his body right to play the next play."

29. Seattle Seahawks, Matayo Uiagalelei, EDGE, Oregon

Reigning Super Bowl champions can go best player available.

30. Baltimore Ravens, Kade Pieper, C, Iowa

They badly need a new center since Tyler Linderbaum left. Why not go back to the same well (the University of Iowa) where they got Linderbaum? Pieper is the highest rate prospect at the position.

31. Buffalo Bills, Austin Siereveld, OG, Ohio State

Bills are going to need to rebuild depth on the interior of the O-line.

32. Cleveland Browns via L.A. Rams, Drake Lindsey , QB, Minnesota

They shouldn't add a new QB. They don't need one. However, a NFL mock draft is more about what you think could happen; instead of what should happen. At 6-5, 230, Lindsey has ideal size for a QB at the next level.

He was extremely efficient and effective in his first full season last year, and should take a leap forward this year.

articles.title: Miami Dolphins find new backup quarterback in Packers' Kyle McCord
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins are going with rookie Jacob Rodriguez over Tyrel Dodson and effectively made a swap of backup QBs as they cut the roster to 53.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins , temporarily carrying just one quarterback as the cut-down deadline in the NFL approached Sunday, swung what could prove to be an important trade, acquiring Green Bay backup quarterback Kyle McCord, who had just thrown four touchdown passes in the preseason finale.

The Dolphins reached the 53-man limit by 6 p.m. Aug. 30 with a series of moves that included cutting veteran linebacker Tyrel Dodson , who started 16 games last season and made 129 tackles. That decision clears the way for second-round pick Jacob Rodriguez to start and settles the key position battle in training camp.

Photos of Miami Dolphins-Atlanta Falcons final NFL preseason game

The Dodson move was the most unexpected of those dropped from the roster. The other major moves involved placing former first-round pick Kenneth Grant, a defensive lineman, and linebacker Trey Moore on injured reserve with a designation to return in a month. They will miss games against the Raiders, 49ers, Chiefs and Vikings but would be eligible to return Oct. 4 vs. Minnesota. Grant has an undisclosed injury; Moore's injury is an ankle.

Other observations on the players making the initial 53-man roster:

Of the 13 players the Dolphins drafted this spring, all remain with the Dolphins, including sixth-rounder DJ Campbell, a guard, and seventh-rounder Max Llewellyn, a defensive end.

Of the 10 unrestricted free agents the team signed, five remain: linebacker Ronnie Harrison Jr., punter Bradley Pinion, receiver Jalen Tolbert, edge rusher Josh Uche and quarterback Malik Willis.

The Dolphins also signed 16 free agents, with six making the roster: long snapper Tucker Addington, safety Zayne Anderson, edge rusher Robert Beal Jr., tackle Marques Cox, edge rusher Clelin Ferrell and tight end Ben Sims. Additionally, cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. was placed on the physically unable to perform list with cornerback Storm Duck.

The Dolphins retained 26 players on offense, 24 on defense and three specialists.

It was a busy weekend for new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan, who traded backup QB Quinn Ewers to Jacksonville and cut Cam Miller, momentarily leaving the Dolphins with Malik Willis as their lone quarterback. But Sullivan turned around and traded for McCord, effectively swapping Ewers for McCord since both trades involved the same 2028 sixth-round pick.

McCord, who turns 24 next month, was a sixth-round pick of Philadelphia in 2025 but has not appeared in an NFL game.

In Green Bay's preseason finale, a 42-38 victory over Arizona, McCord completed 22 of 35 passes for 226 yards, four touchdowns, no interceptions and a 119.5 passer rating.

"He did a heck of a job," coach Matt LaFleur said. " … I think he definitely has the demeanor, no doubt about it. He's in total control out there."

Backup quarterback had been an issue for the Dolphins this summer. Mark Gronowski was cut and then re-signed. Ewers missed time with a groin injury. Cam Miller tended to force the ball. Combined in the three preseason games, the trio didn't lead any touchdown drives and had zero touchdown passes, three interceptions and a 34.2 passer rating.

McCord's name should be familiar to football fans in South Florida. While playing for Syracuse in 2024, he threw for 380 yards and three touchdowns to beat Miami 42-38 and knock the No. 6 Hurricanes out of ACC title contention. He rallied the Orange from a 21-0 deficit.

Dolphins add QB Kyle McCord, meet Malik Willis' new backup

McCord finished that season with 4,779 passing yards, 34 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. The previous season at Ohio State, he threw for 3,170 yards, 24 touchdowns and six interceptions. During his four-year collegiate career, McCord had 61 touchdown passes against 20 interceptions.

While at Syracuse, McCord had a weekly radio show and his own line of honey barbecue cheddar potato chips made by Terrell's.

McCord grew up in New Jersey and chose jersey No. 6 "because of Mark Sanchez," he once said of the former Jets QB.

Before the 2025 draft, NFL.com analyst wrote this scouting report on McCord:

"Pocket passer with good size who played in a high-volume, pro-passing scheme that should give him a head start as a pro. McCord was too inconsistent at Ohio State, relative to the talent around him, but he proved to be confident and productive last season at Syracuse without that same level of supporting talent. His fundamentals are usually solid and he plays with adequate poise in the face of pressure. He has enough arm to make window throws and push the ball around the field.

"McCord seeks to attack coverages vertically instead of operating as a 'Checkdown Charlie.' While he can hit chunk throws, his decision-making and ball placement aren't always good fits for his gunslinger mentality. His mobility inside and outside the pocket is average. McCord has good size, adequate talent and commendable resilience. He could find a home as a backup quarterback with modest upside."

Hal Habib covers the Miami Dolphins for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at HHabib@usatodayco.com.

articles.title: Arizona Cardinals set 53-man roster on 2026 NFL cut day: See the team
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals announced their 53-man roster on Sunday, Aug. 30, with running back James Conner opening the year on IR, among other key moves.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals announced their final 53-man roster on Sunday, Aug. 30, trimming down from the 90 players included on their preseason roster shortly after the NFL's 3 p.m. deadline.

The roster release was most notable for the injury status of James Conner, who was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return. That means he must miss the first four weeks of the season and is not eligible to practice during that span.

Conner, who suffered a season-ending foot injury last September, returned to practice early in training camp but only participated in individual drills, never gearing up to a point where he was able to join full-team work.

See Arizona Cardinals' 53-man roster for 2026 season

Meanwhile, tight end Tip Reiman remained on the physically unable to perform list with a severe foot injury suffered last October. Earlier in the summer, there was optimism that Reiman could return in time for Week 1, but that will not be the case.

Like Conner, Reiman must miss the first four weeks of the season. The difference is that teams can activate only eight players from IR during the season. Reiman, on PUP, does not count toward that limit.

Elsewhere, the Cardinals remade their cornerbacks room, waiving Sean Murphy-Bunting and Starling Thomas V. Those two served as the Cardinals' starting cornerbacks for much of the 2024 season, but both suffered torn ACLs ahead of the 2025 season. Despite returning to full health, neither could regain his starting spot this summer.

Murphy-Bunting's release was especially surprising, as he had worked as the starting nickel cornerback for much of training camp. That move suggests that Garrett Williams — who was activated off PUP earlier this month — is nearing full strength ahead of Week 1. Kei'Trel Clark figures to serve as his backup in the slot.

Also at cornerback, the Cardinals released 2024 third-round pick Elijah Jones, in a widely-expected move. Edge rusher B.J. Ojulari — a 2023 second-round pick — was another former top pick with whom the Cardinals cut ties. Neither player had managed to establish themselves with the organization, as both were marred by injuries and underperformance.

The work, though, isn't done yet for general manager Monti Ossenfort. The Cardinals have 16 spots on their practice squad to fill, either by re-signing players they waived or adding external players once others clear waivers.

Plus, the Cardinals hold the No. 3 waiver claim, by virtue of their 3-14 record last season. They could use that priority to add a player along the defensive front, where their limited depth is especially glaring.

Until then, here is a look at the roster.

Quarterback (3): Jacoby Brissett, Gardner Minshew, Carson Beck

Running back (3): Jeremiyah Love, Tyler Allgeier, Bam Knight

Wide receiver (7): Marvin Harrison Jr., Michael Wilson, Kendrick Bourne, Devin Duvernay, Reggie Virgil, Jalen Brooks, Simi Fehoko

Tight end (3): Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins, Hunter Long

Offensive tackle (4): Paris Johnson Jr., Elijah Wilkinson, Josh Fryar, Jayden Williams

Interior offensive line (5): Isaac Seumalo, Hjalte Froholdt, Isaiah Adams, Jon Gaines, Hayden Conner

Interior defensive line (6): Walter Nolen, Darius Robinson, Roy Lopez, Dante Stills, L.J. Collier, Andrew Billings

Edge rusher (5): Josh Sweat, Baron Browning, Zaven Collins, Jordan Burch, Eku Leota

Inside linebacker (4): Mack Wilson, Jack Gibbens, Cody Simon, Karson Sharar

Cornerback (5): Will Johnson, Garrett Williams, Max Melton, Denzel Burke, Kei'Trel Clark

Safety (5): Budda Baker, Andrew Wingard, Dadrion Taylor-Demerson, Kitan Crawford, Wydett Williams Jr.

articles.title: Buffalo Bills 2026 practice squad tracker
articles.summary: Stay up to date with all the latest Buffalo Bills practice squad news here.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are still in the midst of reducing their roster from a summer high of 91 players down to the league-mandated 53-man active roster for Week 1, where all that's likely left at this point is the official reporting process. The regular season is just around the corner, which means new head coach Joe Brady must have assembled the best active roster he can in hopes of Buffalo claiming a road win opening weekend against the Houston Texans.

It's a huge first task for Brady and company, given the franchise's historical struggles in NRG Stadium — the Bills have never won in the Texans' cozy house. But for a team that has Super Bowl aspirations with quarterback Josh Allen at the helm, there's no time like the present. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook believe that to be true , currently listing the Bills with the best odds of making the playoffs in the AFC (-330), and the second-best odds (+1000) of winning Super Bowl LXI.

The bulk of roster cuts are in the rearview mirror and the waiver-wire process is actively playing out still with a deadline of 1 p.m. EDT on Monday, August 31. Buffalo is 26 in the waiver-wire claim process (based of 2025 NFL standings). But the waiver wire is only part of the equation. It's important to remember that veteran players who are not subject to waivers can immediately negotiate with teams or sign with a practice squad.

The Bills undoubtedly hope to bring back as many of their own released players as possible. But they may also have their radar attuned to other team's cuts for a player they coveted in the draft, as an undrafted rookie free agent, or even a vested veteran. As such, this tracker seeks to keep Bills Mafia up to date with any practice squad news, which will include rumors about potential signings.

Sara Larson has put together a great article with some of finer detailed rules for the practice squad as it pertains to the Bills. That, in addition to the notes below should keep you up to date with how the process works.

Teams can begin forming their practice squads after the waiver period expires at 1 p.m. EDT on Monday, August 31. The NFL will send a subsequent Personnel Notice confirming the results of the waiver process, and teams can begin signing practice squad players after receiving that notice.

A player claimed off waivers cannot go directly to a practice squad. A successful waiver claim means that player goes onto the claiming team's 53-man roster. The player must first clear waivers before becoming eligible to sign with a practice squad.

A standard practice squad consists of 16 players. Teams can have a 17th player if that player qualifies for and is designated under the NFL's International Player Pathway Program. The Bills have reportedly released offensive-lineman-turned-defensive-lineman Travis Clayton (IPP player).

Players who are not subject to waivers can immediately sign with another team or join a practice squad. Players with four or more accrued seasons are unrestricted free agents when released and are not subject to waivers. Players with three or fewer accrued seasons are subject to the waiver process.

the NFL's standard elevation mechanism allows practice squad players to be moved to the active roster for a game and subsequently return to the practice squad without immediately being subjected to waivers, subject to the league's elevation limits.

For purposes of an accrued season, a player generally needs to be on full pay status for at least six regular-season games. That includes time on a club's active/inactive list or certain reserve lists like IR and PUP.

Waived Bills players who can sign to the practice squad

Every team's practice squad changes throughout the season (and playoffs). Players may routinely find themselves signed, released, or elevated to the active roster depending on team needs week to week. That means this list should be view only as an initial group rather than a list of practice squad players set in stone.

Think you've got what it takes to make a play with the Buffalo Bills in 2026? Head over to FanDuel Sportsbook now to put it to the test !

articles.title: Steelers, Eagles, Vikings Among NFL Teams to Keep 4 QBs on 53-Man Roster After Cutdown Deadline
articles.summary: Four NFL teams made the decision to keep four quarterbacks on their 53-man rosters Sunday, a fairly rare occurrence in the modern NFL.
articles.body:
Four NFL teams made the decision to keep four quarterbacks on their 53-man rosters Sunday, a fairly rare occurrence in the modern NFL.

Philadelphia Eagles: Jalen Hurts, Tanner McKee, Andy Dalton, Cole Payton

Atlanta Falcons: Tua Tagovailoa, Michael Penix Jr., Cooper Rush, Jack Strand

Pittsburgh Steelers: Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Will Howard, Drew Allar

Minnesota Vikings: Kyler Murray, J.J. McCarthy, Carson Wentz, Max Brosmer

The Eagles are perhaps the biggest surprise, given that Hurts is both a short- and long-term guarantee to remain the starter. The backup battle between Dalton and McKee will seemingly continue into the regular season, while Payton is perhaps an option to be used on special teams given his inclusion on the roster.

In Atlanta, short-term questions about the position perhaps led to keeping four quarterbacks, while both the Steelers and Vikings seemed to make decisions keeping in mind their longer-term prospects given uncertainty at the position beyond the 2026 season.

articles.title: Rams Troll Heat Over LeBron James YouTube Video Post After Aaron Donald Signs New Contract
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams had a hilarious callback on social media after signing Aaron Donald on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams had a hilarious callback on social media after signing Aaron Donald on Sunday.

The Rams referenced the Miami Heat's accidental YouTube livestream link teasing LeBron James' signing.

Before James joined the Philadelphia 76ers, the Heat posted a YouTube livestream titled "LeBron James Introductory Press Conference," which was quickly deleted.

James, of course, didn't sign with the Heat, and the team explained that the link was a placeholder in the event James did sign with Miami.

The Rams don't have to worry about jinxing Donald's return, though, as he signed a one-year, $20 million deal to come out of retirement and join Los Angeles as it looks to win another Super Bowl.

articles.title: Trevon Diggs' Future Revealed in New NFL Rumors After CB Was Part of Seahawks' Roster Cuts
articles.summary: Trevon Diggs was hoping to revive his NFL career with the Seattle Seahawks, but he won't start the 2026 campaign on the roster.
articles.body:
Trevon Diggs was hoping to revive his NFL career with the Seattle Seahawks, but he won't start the 2026 campaign on the roster.

Diggs did not make the 53-man roster ahead of cuts on Sunday, but the team plans to bring him back on the practice squad, according to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero .

Diggs was an All-Pro player with the Dallas Cowboys in 2021 when he had 11 interceptions, and he put together another strong campaign in 2022, but injuries derailed his career from there. In 2023, he appeared in just two games before suffering a season-ending torn ACL.

Diggs played well in 2024, recording 42 tackles and two interceptions, but his season ended prematurely after 11 games. Last year, he missed a significant portion of the season because of lingering concussion symptoms, and the Cowboys released him in December.

Diggs finished the 2025 season with the Green Bay Packers.

The Seahawks signed Diggs earlier this month, giving him the chance to earn a spot on the roster ahead of the season. He had a strong showing in the preseason, picking up an interception against the Kansas City Chiefs last week, but he didn't do enough to make the 53-man roster.

"He's really come up to speed, which is saying something," Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said . "And I think our players have done a great job of coaching him up and you hear him in walkthroughs, our guys coach him up, play to play, and he knows ball. All it is, is just kind of connecting dots and connecting some of that, all the things that he's heard to the new techniques, the new words and stuff. So did some great things today. Obviously to have the interception was pretty awesome."

Diggs won't get the chance to prove himself in games to start the year, but he could very well be called up to the 53-man roster at some point this season.

articles.title: Aaron Donald channels Michael Jordan in announcing his NFL return with 2 words
articles.summary: Greatness is now the only acceptable outcome for the Rams this season. For a player of Donald's caliber, taking those expectations head on is the only way.
articles.body:
The three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year isn't shying away from expectations. With two words on Sunday, Donald addressed those expectations head on.

Shortly after the news broke that Donald was returning to the Rams on a one-year, $20 million contract , the Rams shared a letter from Donald to NFL commissioner Roger Goodell announcing his return. The body of Donald's letter was concise:

While efficiently getting the point across, Donald's message is a not-so-veiled homage to the greatest athlete comeback in sports history.

In 1995, Michael Jordan sent a fax to media through his agent, David Stern, announcing his comeback to the Chicago Bulls following a 17-month hiatus from basketball to pursue professional baseball.

Like Donald's on Sunday, the body of Jordan's message read, simply: "I'm back."

Jordan went on to play three-plus more seasons with the Bulls. Those seasons produced the second championship three-peat of Jordan's career and cemented his spot as the greatest basketball of player of all time and arguably the greatest athlete in U.S. history.

That's a high bar, even for a player of Donald's caliber. Nothing that Donald does this season or in any subsequent would place him alongside Jordan in the pantheon of sports.

But the message is clear. Donald is returning to to play alongside Myles Garrett for the Rams in pursuit of further greatness. His return, in fact, sets greatness as the only acceptable outcome in Los Angeles. A Rams team that was favored to win the Super Bowl without him is now about as big of a preseason favorite as a team can be .

It sets up an enormous amount of pressure in Los Angeles. For a player of Donald's caliber, facing that pressure head on is the only way.

articles.title: Everything Aaron Donald Said About Signing Rams Contract for NFL Return, Myles Garrett, More
articles.summary: Aaron Donald is back with the Los Angeles Rams after signing a one-year, $20 million deal on Sunday.
articles.body:
Aaron Donald is back with the Los Angeles Rams after signing a one-year, $20 million deal on Sunday.

Donald took to the podium on Sunday evening to offer some insight into his decision, and he pointed to the successful offseason the Rams had, which included a trade for Myles Garrett.

"Seeing what was being done with this team… the pieces that were brought here," he told reporters.

Donald likely wouldn't have returned if he didn't feel the Rams had a chance to make it to the Super Bowl, and the fact that the game will be played in Los Angeles made a comeback even more enticing.

"Super Bowl being back at SoFi kind of excites you, too," he told reporters .

Donald also clarified that he wouldn't have returned if his wife hadn't wanted him to.

"If the wife wasn't happy it wasn't gonna get done," he said . "My wife was on board and she was with me 100%."

It's been a while since Donald played in an NFL game, but he hasn't let himself get out of shape. He's also been working towards a return for most of the summer.

According to ESPN's Sarah Barshop , once Los Angeles traded for Garrett, Donald began putting himself through a "very strict, regimented process that was similar to what he did when he played," so he should be prepared to make an impact immediately.

That said, head coach Sean McVay hasn't made a decision about whether Donald will be on the field for the team's season opener against the San Francisco 49ers next Thursday.

Donald also got a two-game roster exemption from commissioner Rodger Goodell, so he won't count towards the 53-man roster until Sept. 11.

In his last NFL season in 2023, Donald recorded 53 tackles and eight sacks, still a very productive player. If he is able to have that kind of success after three years away, the Rams' defense is going to be one for the ages.

But even if Donald isn't the player he once was, Los Angeles still has arguably the best defensive front with Garrett leading the way. Combine that with a tremendous offense, and Donald's first season back in Los Angeles could end with a Super Bowl victory.

articles.title: “I was ultimately trying to see both”: How Donna Kelce’s 1,300-mile journey to Jason and Travis Kelce’s games became an unforgettable mother-son moment
articles.summary: NFL News: Donna Kelce had two sons playing playoff football on January 16, 2022, and their games were nearly 1,300 miles apart. Jason Kelce’s Philadelphia Eagle.
articles.body: Donna Kelce had two sons playing playoff football on January 16, 2022, and their games were nearly 1,300 miles apart. Jason Kelce’s Philadelphia Eagles faced the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Florida, while Travis Kelce’s Kansas City Chiefs hosted the Pittsburgh Steelers that night. Donna did not pick one son. She watched Jason first, then raced across the country to reach Travis.It was a hectic trip from start to finish. Donna dealt with a rickshaw, an Uber, a delayed flight and rain before reaching Kansas City. She arrived during the Chiefs game, but the long day gave her something far more memorable than a simple trip between stadiums. It gave her a chance to be there for both sons.How did Donna Kelce make it from Jason Kelce’s Eagles game to Travis Kelce’s Chiefs game?Donna began January 16 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, where Jason Kelce and the Eagles faced Tom Brady and the Buccaneers in the NFC Wild Card round. Philadelphia struggled from the start and eventually fell 31-15, ending Jason's season. Donna, however, could not stay in Tampa for long.Travis Kelce and the Chiefs were scheduled to play the Pittsburgh Steelers at Arrowhead Stadium that evening. The Eagles kicked off at 1 p.m. ET, while Kansas City's game started at 8:15 p.m. ET, leaving Donna only a few hours to get from Florida to Missouri.After Jason's game, Donna began the second leg of her journey. She told the NFL that she had to use a rickshaw to reach her Uber pickup area at the stadium. Her flight then faced a 30-minute delay, and rain made the trip even more difficult. Still, Donna kept moving and eventually reached Kansas City.The NFL followed her journey throughout the day. At one point, Donna wrote, “One game down, one to go! Headed to the airport!” She later updated fans from the car on the way to Arrowhead.Donna finally made it into the stadium during the Chiefs game. She missed Travis' 48-yard touchdown catch just before halftime because she was still traveling, but she arrived in time to watch the rest of his impressive night. Travis finished with five catches for 108 yards and a touchdown as Kansas City beat Pittsburgh 42-21. He also threw a two-yard touchdown pass to Byron Pringle in the fourth quarter. Why did Travis Kelce’s postgame exchange with Donna make the journey unforgettable?After the Chiefs' win on January 16, Donna still had one more moment with Travis. She appeared during his postgame news conference and was introduced as the next person to ask a question. Travis initially sounded confused before realizing his mother was on the call.Donna asked how it felt to throw his first NFL touchdown. The question took Travis back to something he had told her as a child.“Man, to finally throw a touchdown like I used to tell my mom when I was like five years old, that I was going to eventually throw a touchdown in the National Football League,” Travis said during the Chiefs' postgame news conference. “I finally got it done, it only took me nine years.”Donna then put the entire day into perspective with her own response. “That's what makes sports so great, because you can be depressed in the morning and elated in the evening,” she told Travis during the postgame exchange.Donna spoke with WKYC's Jay Crawford about the journey. She explained that the goal had always been simple.“I was ultimately trying to see both of the games and it worked out,” Donna said during the WKYC interview.It did. She watched Jason Kelce's Eagles in Tampa, then crossed the country to see Travis Kelce's Chiefs in Kansas City. Jason's team lost, Travis' team won, but Donna never treated the two games differently. For her, the victory was simply making sure both sons saw their mother in the stands that day.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “Please keep him inside”: NFL fans send quirky response as Aaron Donald’s wife Erica gives 7-word remark following Rams star’s NFL return
articles.summary: NFL News: Aaron Donald's wife Erica had jokes loaded the moment the offseason's biggest rumor turned into real news. Three years removed from a Super Bowl ring .
articles.body: Aaron Donald's wife Erica had jokes loaded the moment the offseason's biggest rumor turned into real news. Three years removed from a Super Bowl ring and two seasons into retirement, the Rams legend is suiting up again, and his own household reacted with more humor than most press conferences manage.The signing closed out months of speculation that started the day Los Angeles landed Myles Garrett, and it wrapped up with a contract, a viral tweet, and a fanbase that hasn't stopped talking about what Erica said next. Here's how it all played out, from the early rumors to Sunday's announcement.Aaron Donald's wife Erica sends hilarious response to Rams star's NFL returnThe story goes back to June 1, when the Rams pulled off a blockbuster trade for defensive end Myles Garrett. The very next day, ESPN's Pat McAfee said on his show that he'd talked to Donald, and the trade had gotten the three-time Defensive Player of the Year thinking about a comeback. Reports of a possible return followed almost immediately. Erica marked the actual announcement with the line everyone had been waiting for, posting on X: "I let him out the house y'all," followed by laughing, blue heart, and heart hands emojis. Former Rams teammate Jalen Ramsey, now with the Steelers, called her "the real MVP."Erica wasn't going to let that slide quietly. She posted on X that same day: "Y'all are hilarious." Rams fans pounced, half-joking and half-pleading, asking her to let Donald come back. She stayed cryptic through the summer, and on Aug. 5, a day after Donald worked out at the team facility, she added: "Yall gotta start getting this stuff right."Rams bring back a three-time Defensive Player of the Year on a one-year dealNearly three months after that first tweet, the Rams made it official. Donald is returning on a one-year, $20 million deal that can climb to $30 million with playoff incentives, teaming up with Garrett, himself a two-time Defensive Player of the Year. According to ESPN Research, that pairing makes the Rams the first team to enter a season with multiple players holding multiple Defensive Player of the Year awards.Donald retired in March 2024 after ten NFL seasons. He's an eight-time first-team All-Pro, a ten-time Pro Bowler, and the 2014 Defensive Rookie of the Year, drafted 13th overall by the then-St. Louis Rams. Head coach Sean McVay had said earlier this month that Donald "earned the right" to take his time on the decision.NFL fans respond to Erica's hilarious commentThe replies came fast. One fan wrote, "yall both getting statues outside of sofi [stadium]." Another begged, "Please keep him inside 😭😭." From rival fans came a different tone entirely: "Ma'am...for the sake of the rest of the NFL...get his ass back in the house."Others leaned into pure dread on behalf of opposing linemen. One post read, "You monster. You realize what you've done?!" Another simply said, "What have you done!???" And one fan admitted, "I'm not a rams fan but might have to peek in a bit. What a DLine they'll have."Whatever the Rams' defense does this fall, Erica already won the offseason.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Could Dak Prescott finally breakthrough and win MVP? ESPN host puts Cowboys QB ahead of Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen
articles.summary: NFL News: Dak Prescott has never lacked big numbers. What he has lacked is the MVP season that turns those numbers into a bigger conversation. Now, ESPN’s Steve.
articles.body: Dak Prescott has never lacked big numbers. What he has lacked is the MVP season that turns those numbers into a bigger conversation. Now, ESPN’s Steven Ruiz believes 2026 could finally be that year. He has picked the Dallas Cowboys quarterback as his MVP choice ahead of regular contenders Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen.The prediction sounds bold after Dallas finished 7-9-1 in 2025. But Prescott still delivered 4,552 passing yards and 30 touchdowns in 17 games. That production gives Ruiz a reason to believe Prescott can take another step. Could Dak Prescott finally make his MVP breakthrough?Ruiz made the case for Prescott on ESPN’s “This Is Football” while discussing his predictions for the 2026 season.“I think this is the year that Dak Prescott finally breaks through and we have that Prescott MVP pick,” Ruiz said on "This Is Football".Ruiz expects Prescott to push beyond the 5,000-yard mark. He also pointed to the talent around him and believes Dallas’ offense can be even better than it was last season.“The case is he’s going to throw for 5,000 yards,” Ruiz said on the show. “Playing in that offense, playing with those two receivers… I think it’s going to be better than last year.”There is some history behind that prediction. Prescott came close to 5,000 yards in 2019, finishing that season with 4,902 yards and 30 touchdowns. He now enters 2026 after another 4,500-plus-yard campaign.Ruiz also thinks Prescott’s MVP case could come down to how Dallas finishes the year.“If they just improve marginally and the Cowboys are in the playoff race… I think Dak has a chance to do that,” Ruiz said on "This Is Football". He argued that recent MVP races often favor quarterbacks who finish the season with their strongest stretch.That could give Prescott a clear path. He does not necessarily need to dominate every week. If the Cowboys are winning when the MVP race heats up, his numbers could carry more weight.Can Dallas’ defense turn Dak Prescott’s numbers into wins?This is where the Cowboys need to help their quarterback. Dallas had the NFL’s top offense in total yards per game in 2025, averaging 403.1. Yet the team still missed the playoffs. Prescott’s 4,552 yards and 30 touchdowns could not overcome the problems on defense.The Cowboys entered the 2026 offseason looking to fix that weakness. They hired Christian Parker as defensive coordinator and added Quinnen Williams, Rashan Gary and Kenny Clark.Prescott also enters the season with a clear target. During his August 2026 appearance on “Up & Adams”, he discussed using “Super Bowl 61” as a daily reminder of his ultimate goal.Mahomes and Allen remain major obstacles. Mahomes already has two MVP awards, while Allen won his first in 2024. Prescott has the numbers to join that group. Now, he needs the Cowboys to give those numbers a winning backdrop.If Dallas improves enough to stay in the playoff race, Ruiz’s prediction may become much harder to dismiss.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “We feel so incredibly loved and celebrated”: Chiefs heiress Gracie Hunt shares heart-touching engagement party moment with Derek Green
articles.summary: NFL News: Gracie Hunt is soaking in the joy of her engagement to Derek Green, and her latest photos give fans a glimpse into the celebration with the people clo.
articles.body: Gracie Hunt is soaking in the joy of her engagement to Derek Green, and her latest photos give fans a glimpse into the celebration with the people closest to them. The Kansas City Chiefs heiress shared several moments from their engagement party, including a touching photo of herself holding Green close while their families enjoyed the special occasion around them.Hunt looked elegant in a white dress, while Green opted for a black coat as they posed together during the celebration. The photos captured everything from intimate moments between the couple to family members enjoying the party, making it clear that the evening was centered around love, togetherness and the beginning of their next chapter.How did Gracie Hunt celebrate her engagement with Derek Green?The engagement party appeared to be a particularly emotional celebration for Hunt and Green as they were surrounded by family and friends who came together to mark their upcoming marriage. In one of the most touching photos, Hunt lovingly holds Derek as the two share quiet moments together.Other photos showed the couple enjoying the festivities alongside their families. articles.title: Nine former Colorado football players earn NFL roster spots
articles.summary: From Travis Hunter’s rising star in Jacksonville to Shedeur Sanders securing a spot in Cleveland, these former Buffaloes standouts successfully navigated fin...
articles.body:
We're less than two weeks from the start of the 2026 NFL season. And with the preseason wrapped up, final cuts have happened for all 32 teams. The front offices and coaching staff for each team have been busy trying to figure out who will stay and who will go.

As for the former Colorado Buffaloes players, nine of them were able to make the final rosters. Here's a list of who made the cut after the 6 p.m. ET deadline.

The former Heisman Trophy winner is looking to take a step forward in his NFL journey. There was no doubt he was a lock to make the Jaguars' roster. We'll see how he performs during his second year in the league. There has been speculation whether he'll be used as a two-way player or pick his primary position. Hunter won't be alone in Duval County. Former CU defensive lineman BJ Green also made the Jags final roster.

Shedeur Sanders becomes the backup in Cleveland

After ending the season as a starter, the former Colorado QB moved into a backup role behind Deshaun Watson, who returns under center after a string of major injuries. The former fifth-rounder is likely to be a starter once again sometime later in the season. For now, the son of Deion Sanders will be on clipboard duty to support Watson and the Browns offense.

Two for Baltimore, including LaJohntay Wester

No real surprise with the Ravens locking up Wester. He had a great preseason and earned his spot on the roster for a second straight season. Baltimore also added former Colorado cornerback Chidobe Awuzie, who also enters his second season for the AFC North contender. In his tenth season, Awuzie has carved out a decent NFL career. One of the few CU players left from the Mike MacIntyre era.

The Panthers suffered a string of injuries at the wide receiver position during the course of the preseason, leaving Horn to pick up the pieces. The former Colorado standout earned his spot on Carolina's final roster and will try to contribute more than his rookie year.

Seattle keeps Colorado & NFL legacy Brady Russell

After winning a Super Bowl, the former Colorado standout two-way player Brady Russell is staying put. His uncle, Matt Russell, was an All-American linebacker at CU. He's also a senior personnel executive for the Philadelphia Eagles.

Landman will be in the City of Angels for another season. He'll be on a stacked Rams defense who just added Aaron Donald. This could be the year LA makes a run for a hometown Super Bowl.

After previous stops in New England and Denver, the former Buffs offensive lineman finds a new home. The Saints will try to give him another look in the league.
